# Were GoFundMe Pro and DonorPerfect hacked?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by both companies' own accounts: GoFundMe says an unauthorized party accessed GoFundMe Pro data; DonorPerfect says it found unauthorized activity and went offline. Who did it, and whether one attacker, is not established.

Incident: GoFundMe Pro and DonorPerfect breaches, Nov 2026. Also reported as GoFundMe Pro data breach, DonorPerfect cyberattack and Nonprofit fundraising platform attacks. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 11:12 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by GoFundMe, DonorPerfect, Salesforce, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 11:12 AM ET: **Both companies confirm unauthorized access; who did it, how, and whether it was one attacker: not established.** First draft. 9 sources (5 Tier 1, 3 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 15 claims (5 Confirmed, 5 Reported, 1 Unverified, 4 Not established), 10 questions. GoFundMe and DonorPerfect each admit unauthorized access on their own status pages (Confirmed). The AI bots and marketing website account, the Salesforce statement, the Salesforce credentials and the notification details are Reported from press quoting the companies. A claim that funds were diverted is Unverified. Counts, DonorPerfect data impact, attacker, same-attacker and any tie to the November outage wave are Not established. We did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker. Corrections to the brief: DonorPerfect has not been offline continuously since Nov 10, it began staged restoration Nov 14 and only the API and mobile app remain down; GoFundMe public notice says donor credentials were not accessed, and card numbers and bank details were not accessed. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles, contact details or phone numbers.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. DonorPerfect says it serves about 11,000 nonprofit customers, and GoFundMe Pro is used by many more, in the weeks before Giving Tuesday. Neither company has said how many people's information is involved, so size rests on the platforms' reach, not a count.
- Who is affected: People whose information sits in GoFundMe Pro, mainly donors and supporters of nonprofits that use it, and the nonprofits' staff. DonorPerfect's customers lost access to the platform for days; whether their donors' data was taken is not established.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 10 | First GoFundMe Pro access | Per GoFundMe's Nov 20 notice |
| Nov 10 | DonorPerfect goes offline | Per its status page |
| 11,000 | DonorPerfect customers | Per the company, to Fortune |

### Known so far

- GoFundMe says an unauthorized third party accessed data from GoFundMe Pro on Oct 10 to 18 and Nov 8 to 9.
- DonorPerfect says it found unauthorized activity and took its application offline on Nov 10.
- GoFundMe says the data included names, postal addresses, phone numbers and, for some, dates of birth.
- GoFundMe's Salesforce connection was cut off and is still disabled.
- DonorPerfect has restored most of its application since Nov 14; its API and mobile app were still down on Nov 21.

### Not known yet

- How many people's information was taken, at either company.
- Whether DonorPerfect customer or donor data was taken.
- How the attackers got into GoFundMe Pro. DonorPerfect says its marketing website, which is its own claim.
- Who did it, and whether it was the same attacker at both.
- Whether the AI bots account is accurate.

## Related, but separate

| Claim | Label | What we know | Why it supports, and more detail | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| These breaches are part of the November 2026 wave of outages | Not established | Fortune lists the DonorPerfect incident alongside the Microsoft, FAA and Chase outages, then says DonorPerfect's was "different" because the company confirmed unauthorized activity. | Timing alone is not evidence. No source ties these two breaches to those outages. The access to GoFundMe Pro began in October. | [Fortune: Nonprofit fundraising platforms like GoFundMe Pro, DonorPerfect are under attack ahead of Giving Tuesday](https://fortune.com/2026/11/21/donorperfect-gofundme-pro-cyberattack-nonprofits-giving-tuesday/) |

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of our latest check on Nov 21.

- A published account of how the attackers got into GoFundMe Pro, or a forensic report from either company. DonorPerfect says the initial access was its marketing website; that is a statement to the press only.
- Independent evidence for the AI bots claim, or an outside expert's review of it.
- Any count of the people affected, from GoFundMe, DonorPerfect, a regulator or an outlet.
- Any statement from DonorPerfect on whether customer or donor data was taken.
- Any named attacker, ransomware or extortion claim, or published data reported by an outlet. We looked only at news coverage and company pages. We did not visit leak sites, dark-web pages or trackers.
- A public Salesforce page for its statement on the GoFundMe Pro connected app; we found it only quoted in The NonProfit Times.
- A public GoFundMe page for its message to customers about Salesforce credentials; we found it only quoted by Fortune and the Chronicle of Philanthropy.
- Any official or independent link to the other November outages.
- The Chronicle of Philanthropy article blocks automated access, so we read its text through a search result, not the page itself. The Nov 20 notice was read on GoFundMe's own status page.
- A security notice on a Classy status page (a GoFundMe product) repeats the same text; we did not find it to say anything different.

GoFundMe and DonorPerfect each admit unauthorized access on their own status pages (Confirmed). The AI bots and marketing website account, the Salesforce statement, the Salesforce credentials and the notification details are Reported from press quoting the companies. A claim that funds were diverted is Unverified. Counts, DonorPerfect data impact, attacker, same-attacker and any tie to the November outage wave are Not established. We did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker. Corrections to the brief: DonorPerfect has not been offline continuously since Nov 10, it began staged restoration Nov 14 and only the API and mobile app remain down; GoFundMe public notice says donor credentials were not accessed, and card numbers and bank details were not accessed. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles, contact details or phone numbers. | Added |
